drill.audience: Just the coach — read it like you're telling it to a friend, not announcing it.
constraints: No stopping or restarting — a flubbed rep is data
When the next word isn't ready, pause a full second instead of repeating the last phrase
drill.name: Sixty Clean
principles: Fillers are discomfort with silence made audible — practice the pause and they starve
Slow down on what's important; one default speed flattens everything
drill.prompt: Talk for 60 seconds about something you learned recently.

fix_carried_forward: Place one pause deliberately before the key line

learn.level_focus: Voice L1 trains continuity, not polish: finish 60 seconds without stopping or restarting. Speed, pace, and polish come later — first, don't stop.
learn.your_pattern: Your filler isn't um or uh — it's repeating the last phrase when the next word isn't ready. Fillers are discomfort with silence made audible; the pause starves them.
during_your_day: When the next word isn't ready, pause a full second instead of repeating the last phrase.
Before the key line in any conversation — the point, the number, the ask — place one deliberate pause.
Slow down on what matters; speed up on the rest. One default speed flattens everything.
After any conversation, ask yourself: did I finish my thought without restarting?
learn.how_feedback_works: Brief → record → predict your pace and fillers before listening back → review → keep exactly one fix → re-drill. Predicting first is what makes the feedback land.
